A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the modern business enterprise is a machine contrived to make the most efficient use of the modern industrial plant, which in its essence consists of an industrial system carried on by a large number of independent business concerns, which are in a state of more or less continuous competition with one another, and in a state of dependence upon one another.

the modern business enterprise is a system of exploitation, and that the modern business man is an exploiter; and that, as a consequence of the nature of his calling, he is in the habit of thinking of the world as a field of exploitation.

the modern industrial system, as we have seen, rests on a system of pecuniary relations, and that this pecuniary system is in the main a matter of convention, of usage, and that it is in this respect unlike any other system of human relations, and unlike the system of mechanical relations on which the material processes are carried on in the industrial system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transaction cost framework of Williamson has not yet been able to explain firm strategies as well as Veblen did in 1904.
there are two main types of firms in the economy, those that are transactionally efficient and those that are not.
Veblen's theory of the evolution of business enterprise is not only a viable theory of business enterprise but a superior theory to Williamson's.
